page: Microsoft Azure E2bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EBDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8370C core with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 KB L1D cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It includes hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It also includes 77 GB of local SSD storage and supports premium block storage.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is moderate, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1647.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance rated as average. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are limited. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the lower percentile, reflecting the physical constraint of having only a single physical core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds measuring 14.85 GB/sec and 13.69 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET performance are relatively low, indicating that while memory capacity is high, throughput-heavy workloads may face bottlenecks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E2bds_v5 provides a dense memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. It is suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, lightweight web serving, and single-threaded data processing tasks. However, it is less suited for heavy multi-threaded compilation, complex physics simulations, or large-scale LLM inference due to its single physical core limitation.
